hazards.name: Space Radiation
hazards.description: Galactic Cosmic Radiation (GCR), Solar Particle Events (SPE), and secondary neutrons penetrating spacecraft shielding.
hazards.operationalImpact: Cumulative carcinogenic risk, central nervous system alterations, acute radiation syndromes during solar proton events.

hazards.name: Isolation & Confinement
hazards.description: Prolonged psychological confinement, small living volumes, lack of circadian natural light, and sensory monotony.
hazards.operationalImpact: Sleep disturbances, mood alteration, cognitive friction, interpersonal conflict, circadian phase misalignment.

hazards.name: Distance from Earth
hazards.description: Increasing one-way communication latency (up to 24+ minutes for Mars), lack of real-time telemedicine, impossible emergency evacuation.
hazards.operationalImpact: Requires complete crew autonomy in clinical triage, medical decision-making, surgical procedures, and resource management.

hazards.name: Altered Gravity Fields
hazards.description: Weightlessness (0g), hypergravity during ascent/entry, and partial gravity (0.38g Mars, 0.16g Moon).
hazards.operationalImpact: Cephalad fluid shift, Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), bone demineralization, muscle atrophy, vestibular disorientation.

hazards.name: Hostile / Closed Environments
hazards.description: Hermetically sealed spacecraft cabin, elevated carbon dioxide (CO2), trace volatile contaminants, acoustic noise, microbial biome accumulation.
hazards.operationalImpact: Hypercapnia headaches, respiratory mucosal irritation, immune hypersensitivity, ECLSS filter saturation, toxic particulate inhalation.

outcomes.name: Cardiovascular Health
outcomes.description: Vascular remodeling, reduced stroke volume, cardiac muscle atrophy, and post-flight orthostatic intolerance.

outcomes.name: Immune Function
outcomes.description: T-cell function suppression, altered cytokine secretion, latent viral reactivation (EBV, VZV), and wound healing delays.

outcomes.name: Bone & Muscle Integrity
outcomes.description: Cancellous bone mineral density decline (1.0-1.5%/month), muscle atrophy, tendon stiffness loss, and hypercalciuria nephrolithiasis risk.

outcomes.name: Vision & SANS
outcomes.description: Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome: optic disc edema, globe flattening, choroidal folds, and hyperopic refractive shifts.

outcomes.name: Cognitive Performance
outcomes.description: Executive function preservation, fine motor reaction speed, dual-task attentional reserve, and spatial orientation.

outcomes.name: Sleep Architecture
outcomes.description: Sleep fragmentation, reduction of slow-wave and REM sleep stages, circadian desynchrony, and daytime fatigue.

outcomes.name: Behavioral & Psychological Health
outcomes.description: Mood stability, stress resilience, coping strategies in extreme confinement, and mission morale.

outcomes.name: Radiation Exposure & Tissue Dose
outcomes.description: Cumulative absorbed dose, effective dose equivalent (mSv), acute tissue micro-lesions, and career toxicity limits.

outcomes.name: General Physiological Adaptations
outcomes.description: Core body temperature elevation ('space fever'), metabolic shifts, red blood cell mass reduction ('space anemia').

connections.healthImpact: Direct cellular DNA double-strand breaks, reactive oxygen species generation, acute lymphoid tissue suppression, and cumulative cancer risk.
connections.scientificEvidence: Extensive empirical measurements across Gemini, Apollo, Skylab, ISS, and BioSentinel missions. Career dose limits established under NASA-STD-3001.
connections.source: NASA Human Research Program — Space Radiation Risk Book
connections.suggestedAction: Continuous dosimeter logging; verify shelter readiness if DONKI reports SPE with proton flux >10 pfu at >10 MeV.

connections.healthImpact: Cephalad fluid shift removes hydrostatic pressure gradients, causing chronically elevated venous pressure at the head, engorged optic sheath, papilledema, and hyperopic shift.
measurements: Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) retinal nerve layer thickness
connections.scientificEvidence: Documented in >60% of long-duration ISS crewmembers. NASA SANS research clinical protocols (HRP SANS Evidence Book).
connections.source: NASA HRP — Risk of SANS / Human System Risks
connections.suggestedAction: Weekly Snellen/LogMAR visual acuity tests; monthly OCT scans; avoid prolonged head-down postures; use lower body negative pressure (LBNP) if prescribed.

connections.healthImpact: Removal of mechanical gravitational loading uncouples osteoblast-osteoclast activity, leading to progressive bone resorption (~1%/month) and postural slow-twitch muscle fiber atrophy.
connections.scientificEvidence: Longitudinal ISS cohort studies comparing pre-ARED vs post-ARED implementation. Demonstrates mechanical strain preserves cortical architecture.
connections.source: NASA Human Research Program — Bone Risk Evidence Report
connections.suggestedAction: Mandatory 2.0-2.5 h/day countermeasure protocol (ARED heavy resistance + CEVIS/T2 aerobic); monitor weekly delivered mechanical load.

connections.healthImpact: Initial central hypervolemia triggers renal fluid excretion, reducing plasma volume by 10-15%. Prolonged reduction in cardiac workload causes left ventricular mass reduction and baroreflex resetting.
connections.scientificEvidence: Consistently documented in spaceflight and bed rest head-down tilt (HDBR) terrestrial analogs across decades.
connections.source: NASA Cardiovascular Laboratory / Human System Risks
connections.suggestedAction: Wearable continuous HRV and resting HR monitoring; fluid loading protocol with electrolyte tablets prior to landing/re-entry.

connections.healthImpact: Lack of natural 24h solar cycle (ISS experiences 16 sunrises/day), acoustic cabin noise, and confinement induce sleep latency elongation and sleep fragmentation.
connections.scientificEvidence: NASA actigraphy and PSG sleep studies on ISS demonstrating average nightly sleep of ~6.0-6.2 hours vs planned 8.0 hours.
connections.source: NASA Behavioral Health & Performance / ISS Lighting Protocols
connections.suggestedAction: Dynamic Solid-State Light Assemblies (SSLA) tuned to blue-depleted warm light 90 min before sleep; strict 8-hour protected sleep schedule.

connections.healthImpact: Chronic psychological confinement and elevated glucocorticoids (cortisol) downregulate cellular immunity, leading to subclinical reactivation of latent herpesviruses.
measurements: Saliva qPCR for EBV and VZV DNA copies
connections.scientificEvidence: Artemis II saliva biomarker research protocols and ISS crew immunology studies by Crucian et al. (NASA JSC).
connections.source: NASA Immunology & Virology / Artemis II Saliva Study
connections.suggestedAction: Scheduled non-invasive saliva sampling (scheduled -> collected -> stored at -80°C); correlate viral titers with psychological stress indices.

connections.healthImpact: Elevated cabin carbon dioxide (CO2 > 3,500-4,000 ppm) combined with poor localized air mixing can cause subtle cerebral vasodilation, headache, and transient executive function fatigue.
measurements: Ambient cabin CO2 partial pressure (ppm / mmHg)
connections.scientificEvidence: NASA ECLSS clinical reports and controlled environmental human chamber studies (Law et al., NASA Technical Reports).
connections.suggestedAction: Daily PVT reaction test; cross-check cognitive drift against environmental scrubber status; maintain cabin CO2 < 3.0 mmHg.

connections.healthImpact: Communication delay (up to 20-40 min roundtrip for Mars) removes real-time Earth guidance during complex emergencies, multiplying cognitive workload and task saturation.
connections.scientificEvidence: NASA human analog missions (HERA, NEEMO, CHAPEA) simulating communication delays up to 22 minutes.
connections.source: NASA Behavioral Health and Performance / Exploration Medical Capability
connections.suggestedAction: Delay-aware decision support (VITASTRA Triage); automated step-by-step checklists; verify local procedure execution without ground confirmation.

connections.healthImpact: Closed spacecraft atmosphere with altered convective cooling and thermal regulation dynamics causes resting core body temperature elevation (~1.0°C higher, termed 'space fever').
connections.scientificEvidence: Thermo-miniature sensor research on ISS (Stahn et al., Scientific Reports / ESA/NASA study).
connections.source: NASA Space Station Cell Studies / Thermo-regulation
connections.suggestedAction: Continuous non-invasive skin/core temperature tracking; differentiate thermoregulatory reset from infectious fever using baseline comparisons.

connections.healthImpact: High-Z and high-energy (HZE) particles in Galactic Cosmic Rays may disrupt hippocampal neurogenesis, synaptic dendritic spines, and neuro-inflammation pathways.
measurements: Biomarkers of neuronal injury (Neurofilament light chain)
connections.scientificEvidence: Brookhaven National Laboratory NASA Space Radiation Laboratory (NSRL) rodent studies and emerging human neural organoid payloads (PMC11631337).
connections.source: NASA Space Radiation Laboratory / Nature Communications
connections.suggestedAction: Quarterly deep-cognitive battery; monitor cumulative radiation dose; never attribute single cognitive dip to radiation without multi-factor analysis.
